summary: This script compares two versions of the same file located in different project folders. It first validates that both folders and files exist, then uses the diff command to show what lines differ between them, printing a success message if they're identical.

explanations.7: [[ ! -d ... ]] checks if the folder does NOT exist (the ! means 'not'). If it doesn't exist, the script prints an error message in red and returns (exits) early.
explanations.8: Same validation as line 7, but checking that the specific file exists inside the source folder.
explanations.12: \033[1;34m are escape codes that make text blue; \033[0m resets the color back to normal. This prints the comparison header in blue.
explanations.13: This prints an informational message using escape codes to color parts of it—red for the source file location and green for the comparison file location.
explanations.15: pushd changes into the source folder (> /dev/null hides the directory change message), diff compares the two files showing only differing lines, then popd returns to the original folder. The && operators mean each command only runs if the previous one succeeded.
